answer: Sybil resistance binds each agent identity to remote attestation of an approved enclave measurement (MRENCLAVE) and a hardware-backed, non-exportable key. MRENCLAVE identifies code, not a unique chip, so the protocol must also verify platform-bound key provenance; a hollow VM clone cannot reproduce that credential, while multiplying identities entails acquiring attested silicon. The cipher protects proofs in transit, and lotus can serve as a human-readable enclave policy label.
